cases.carrier:
Hey, I meant to text you earlier but kept getting sidetracked with weeds. The tomatoes finally started climbing up that trellis we stuck by the corner today—looks ridiculous, but way better than before. I swear half of them are ready to explode already, and I’ve been picking the green ones before breakfast just so they don’t. Not gonna lie when one lands on your porch next.

You up with those weird food preferences of yours this week? I still can’t wrap my head around how you eat a whole pickle with a glass and then drink it back out… where am I missing that? Speaking of weird habits? I may have turned on all those mystery channels on YouTube for a minute the other night to distract from the fact I forgot whether the dishes were in the dishwasher.

Anyway. I should check the weather before we talk too much—if I promise a roadtrip within a few weeks I should probably be honest how often that’ll turn into a 2 am phone-call “let me just take pictures of the weird clouds.”

How’s the job hunt going? I keep forgetting you’re even *in the middle* of it. Last time I checked, your brain still worked too well for “regular,” let me know how that’s holding up. And seriously, if things get bad, you can always just ask someone at my job how much they actually think about me while counting paper. (Disclaimer: not that I’d ask, or do it myself, or whatever.) Probably the most honest salary check a guy’s ever given. No joke though, I should probably call that place just for my health.

—

Oh. Wait. You’re still doing karaoke at That Bar? I should come one weekend soon. Just don’t tell me the “funny story” part where [last musician] gets in trouble anymore. I think my ears have adjusted at this point. But let’s go anyway, okay. My tolerance of bad music went from almost zero to whatever the bar keeps alive—something to prove. (I’m guessing you won last Friday already. No shame, it is what it’s always gonna be.)—that thing. You owe me an explanation for how you sing “Bohemian Rhapsody” without looking like you’re about to cry.

Let me know when you’re free to talk, or just send a meme. I’ll be here.

—Jake

cases.carrier:
Hey you, hope this finds you in a good headspace.

I took my first real solo train ride this week—something I’ve been meaning to do for ages but kept putting off until last-minute tickets were like digging for buried treasure. Got on an Amtrak up north, all by myself, and spent half the time talking myself out of panicking I’d end up stranded in some abandoned station or something. Turns out, most of it actually felt kinda cool: that whole *get in, zone out, enjoy the chaos of strangers’ conversations* thing. Then spent a few hours in these weird diners by the waystations just watching trains pull up every 20 minutes or something, waiting for the "main event" train I boarded.

What you’ve got goin’ on these days? Any more weird hikes or deep forest conversations going on? I swear there should be one big thing I’m still hearing about but you haven’t dropped at all… or maybe it’s the other way around? You *got* any more random life upheavals brewing behind that composed mask? Tell me what I can do to ruin your day—or help you forget mine. That old routine still exists.

(I’m jokingly threatening to tell Aunt Karen about what happens when someone leaves a beer under the seat of their friend’s recliner for, like, *ten years*. You’ve always sworn you’ll deny everything. She would. And would still know. Just ask me.) Always here to debate the ethics of that crime—if there even is one—when you want (or force you onto) the topic, as usual.

P.S. Your voicemail still has that *dang* elevator music ringtone. Is it working on you yet? Or just a slow poison? Either way—good choice if it’s making you lose sleep… though that’s a low bar anyway. We can get you to change the music of life. Eventually (when you’re ready). Or if I have to pry the phone from your hands first and shatter the phone with our own fists, so be it. I love you. *No pressure.* Don’t think about it. That way. Laugh, and we can move on. Probably. You’ll tell me tomorrow when I bring it up in like 4 years.

—Jamie

cases.carrier:
I was looking at the schedule this afternoon and realized we’ve got a pretty wide-open weekend—something feels a little light, even though we always fill it up. Figured we could grab dinner with everyone again this Saturday; there’s been a spot at my place’s kitchen table open for a while, which is weird because the group just vibes. No real agenda either, but we’ve got extra beets in the freezer just in case, and they always keep the wine on ice.

What are your plans this week at this point? Just checking in because your last text felt abrupt, so I wondered if we missed the loop. Not that anything’s broken; this whole year has a way of drifting us toward quieter spaces anyway. Maybe after we eat there’s space in your car for that one side trip we’ve mentioned. It’s easy enough to just go somewhere quiet though and let time take itself out—you used to love doing that. Or don’t, though; not pressure. Just thinking out loud like I can’t shake it off before hitting “send.” But I did send so let’s pretend like nothing’s up to now. Anyway, see you at some point sometime today to run that list you started. There really wasn’t a hurry, but your house just happens to have a printer. You do know that about me better than my own schedule. Probably. By now it makes sense though. So probably. You’ll remember the rest in a bit anyways. I just need a second. Or three minutes of silence. But this way I still feel like I wrote something even if half of it wasn’t real. Wait: real is whatever you remember. There was always real. I do trust I remembered. Maybe you’ll remember I asked. We might even just hang around somewhere until you do. I hope I haven’t made you wonder now, because you already have too many things wondering and some of them shouldn’re thinking this much in advance. Anyway that’s fine though; your mind always thinks a lot ahead and a little late, and by the day of I just want to be there. I’ll see you soon.

Let me know if you’re up for it, or if you’d rather just say no and I’ll understand. I’ll be here.

Jake
